tool_calls.arguments:
{"sql":"SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name,
       ROUND(AVG(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 2) AS avg_minutes,
       COUNT(t.TrackId) AS track_count
FROM MediaType m
LEFT JOIN Track t USING (MediaTypeId)
GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name
ORDER BY m.MediaTypeId;"}

I computed the mean track length (in minutes) for each media type by averaging the Track.Milliseconds values and converting to minutes. Results (MediaTypeId — Name — average minutes — track count):

1 — MPEG audio file — 4.43 min (3034 tracks)
2 — Protected AAC audio file — 4.70 min (237 tracks)
3 — Protected MPEG-4 video file — 39.05 min (214 tracks)
4 — Purchased AAC audio file — 4.35 min (7 tracks)
5 — AAC audio file — 4.61 min (11 tracks)

Note: I used the arithmetic mean of Milliseconds converted to minutes and rounded to 2 decimal places. Media types 4 and 5 have small track counts, so their averages are less stable than the larger groups.
sql_used:
SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name,
       ROUND(AVG(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 2) AS avg_minutes,
       COUNT(t.TrackId) AS track_count
FROM MediaType m
LEFT JOIN Track t USING (MediaTypeId)
GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name
ORDER BY m.MediaTypeId;
assumptions: "Average track length" interpreted as the arithmetic mean of Track.Milliseconds converted to minutes; results rounded to 2 decimal places.
Include all media types (LEFT JOIN) so media types with zero tracks would appear (none do here).
